subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: For systemd-managed Gateway turns, should config `env.KIMI_API_KEY` be treated as an effective runtime credential, or should durable provider credentials be required in the per-agent auth profile store with `models status` labeling config env as CLI/config-only?
rationale: Both choices touch auth-provider behavior, daemon secret materialization, status semantics, and docs; the repo policy treats auth/config/default changes as compatibility-sensitive, so automation should not pick the credential contract alone.

options.title: Support config env in managed Gateway
options.body: Materialize or apply config env in the managed Gateway runtime path, then prove systemd Kimi turns and status agree without writing secrets into unsafe surfaces.

options.title: Require auth profiles for daemon turns
options.body: Keep systemd service env minimal, update docs and `models status --agent` to distinguish config-only env from managed-runtime auth, and steer users to per-agent API-key profiles.

options.title: Split status and runtime semantics
options.body: Keep current runtime behavior but change status output to warn when an env credential is visible only to the CLI process and not proven in the managed Gateway runtime.

recommendation.title: Support config env in managed Gateway
recommendation.body: Materialize or apply config env in the managed Gateway runtime path, then prove systemd Kimi turns and status agree without writing secrets into unsafe surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The current blame and recent review history point to Vincent across the active config, gateway startup, service-env marker, daemon install, and status surfaces.
